title: Vericoding for Rust vs. Lean 4: Does Verus-Style Verification Outperform Lean for Security Code?

original_idea.body:
# Vericoding for Rust vs. Lean 4: Does Verus-Style Verification Outperform Lean for Security Code?

**Problem:** Verus (Rust-based formal verification) and Lean 4 are both active formal verification targets for LLMs. Whether Verus-style verification (closer to systems programming) achieves higher LLM success rates for security-critical code than Lean 4 is unknown.

**Direction:** Select 30 security-critical algorithm implementations (buffer handling, crypto, input parsing). Run AlphaVerus (Verus target) and a Lean 4 pipeline on the same problems. Measure compilation rate, proof success, and — crucially — whether the security properties captured differ between the two frameworks.

**Why it matters:** Rust is increasingly used for security-critical systems code. If Verus (Rust-native verification) achieves higher LLM success than Lean 4 for security-relevant programs, it may be a better fit for the RAND vision of verified security code.

**Relevant context:** AlphaVerus achieves 38% on HumanEval-Verified in Verus. Lean 4 Self-Optimizing Agent achieves 60%. But these are different benchmarks. A direct head-to-head comparison on security-relevant tasks does not exist.
